question: tanong lang po, the car just clicks when i turn the key
ai_answer:
Direct answer: A repeated clicking or popping noise when turning, especially during tight turns while accelerating, is a classic sign of a worn outer CV (constant-velocity) joint on a front-wheel-drive or all-wheel-drive car. It is often caused by a torn CV boot that let the grease out and dirt in. Other parts can also make noises when turning, so it needs an inspection to confirm.

Possible causes and mechanisms: A worn outer CV joint, usually after its rubber boot has torn. Worn wheel bearings, suspension joints or strut mounts. Loose brake or suspension hardware, or something rubbing the wheel.

Clues that help distinguish causes: Clicking that gets faster with speed in a tight turn; grease splattered around the inside of the wheel; vibration when accelerating can point to an inner CV joint.

Safe preliminary checks: Look behind the front wheels for a torn rubber boot or grease spray, with the engine off and the car parked safely. Note which side the noise comes from and whether it happens turning left, right or both.

Next steps: Have it inspected soon. A badly worn CV joint can fail and leave the car unable to drive; loud clunking or vibration when accelerating is more urgent.

This is general information, not a confirmed diagnosis or a determination that the vehicle is safe to drive.
